name: instead
why: A Russian-origin text adventure interpreter with its own old-school engine, an unusual environment worth exploring.

brief.what_it_is: INSTEAD is a free interpreter for text adventure games, the Russian-origin engine that runs games written as simple text-based interactive fiction. The homepage describes the genre as sitting between interactive literature, visual novels and classic point-and-click adventures, and says games are written in Lua. You feed it a game (an unzipped folder in ~/.instead/games/, a zipped game file passed on the command line, or a file picked with F4) and it plays the game on screen. It is MIT-licensed and the homepage lists Windows, Linux, macOS, Android and web as targets. The homepage also says it can be used as a simple 2D engine.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents it as a tool for making text-graphic adventure games, with a claim that it has good Russian-language documentation. The README is terse and gives no separate motivation.
brief.how_it_works: Game logic is written in Lua and run by the INSTEAD interpreter, which loads a game from a directory or a zip archive. The README says the program runs zip-packed games directly. Developer docs ship with the distribution in a doc/ directory, and the homepage notes that the game editor should use UTF-8 without BOM.

commands_seen.context: Runs a zip-packed INSTEAD game directly from the command line (from the README's 'Install games' section).

brief.install_notes: Beyond brew install, the README says to run games you can unzip the game archive into ~/.instead/games/, run a zip-packed game with the command above, or press F4 inside the program to open a file dialog. The homepage offers prebuilt downloads for Windows, Linux AppImage, macOS (x86_64 and arm) and Android, and source code. The README points to an INSTALL file for build instructions, which I did not fetch. The homepage lists a separate sdl-instead executable in the brew formula, which I did not verify.
brief.standout: Games are plain Lua scripts loaded from folders or zips, so the engine is small and the authoring format is open. The homepage also mentions an engine-level parser called МЕТАПАРСЕР3 (Metaparser 3) and a 10-year indie project article, though I did not read those pages.
brief.status: Probably maintained, though I could not confirm dates. The homepage lists INSTEAD 3.6.0 as the current download, with 3.5.x and 3.4.1 entries before it, and the README has a CI build badge. The master branch is noted as building against SDL3 with the SDL2 branch kept separately. No release dates were visible.
brief.caveats: The homepage and most documentation are in Russian; the README is in English. The README warns that master builds only against SDL3 and that SDL2 users must use the SDL2 branch. Games are authored in Lua and need UTF-8 without BOM. The homepage's download list does not include a Homebrew or package-manager route, and the brew formula's own description is a single line with no caveats.

judge.reason: A niche Russian text-graphic adventure engine whose Lua-authored games bridge interactive fiction and visual novels offers an unusual format to explore.

entry.title: INSTEAD
entry.tldr: A small Lua-driven interpreter for text adventures from the Russian interactive fiction scene. Hand it a zipped game and it plays.
entry.deeper_look:
INSTEAD is an interpreter for text adventure games. It loads a game from a folder or a zip archive and plays it in a window with text, and optionally pictures and sound. The homepage places the genre somewhere between interactive literature, visual novels and classic point-and-click adventures. It also says the engine can serve as a simple 2D engine.

Games are written in Lua. The engine is small and the authoring format is open: a game is a plain script plus assets, not a compiled binary. You can unzip a game into `~/.instead/games/`, pass a zip on the command line, or press F4 inside the program to pick a file.

The project comes out of the Russian-language interactive fiction community, and that shows. The homepage and most documentation are in Russian, and the homepage claims good Russian-language documentation for authors. It also mentions a parser layer called Metaparser 3, though the brief did not cover it. The README is in English but terse. Developer docs ship with the distribution in a `doc/` directory.

The idea underneath is that a whole game can be a readable script that a tiny runtime interprets. That makes it a way into how interactive fiction engines are built, and into a corner of the genre that most English-language players have never seen.
entry.install:
brew install instead
# Needs a game to play: INSTEAD does not ship with one in the brief. Get a game zip from the project site or the community.

try_this.what_happens: Runs a zip-packed INSTEAD game directly, with no unpacking needed.
Opens the interpreter without a game; press F4 to pick a game file from a dialog.

entry.whats_unique: Games are plain Lua scripts in folders or zips, so the engine stays small and the format is open. It is also a window into a Russian-language interactive fiction scene.
entry.caveats: The homepage and most documentation are in Russian, master builds only against SDL3 (SDL2 users need a separate branch), and you must find games to play yourself.
